text_summary.body: Jeremiah 46:2 heads an oracle about Egypt by identifying the army of Pharaoh Necho that Nebuchadnezzar defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates, dating the defeat to the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah.

setting.period: Late Iron Age; end of the Assyrian-Egyptian alliance (609–605 BC)
setting.body: After the fall of Nineveh and Harran, Egypt under Necho II held the upper Euphrates. In Nabopolassar's 21st year (605) the crown prince Nebuchadnezzar crossed the river, defeated the Egyptian army at Carchemish, pursued its remnants into the district of Hamath, and then returned to Babylon on his father's death to take the throne on 1 Ululu (7 Sep 605).

rulers.role: Babylonian commander (crown prince), king from Sep 605
Egyptian king whose army was defeated

competing_reconstructions.summary: Whether Carchemish (Mar–Aug 605) falls in Jehoiakim's "fourth year" depends on how Jeremiah counted Jehoiakim's years and on when in 609 Jehoiakim acceded. Each reckoning option is computed by the chronology engine.

open_questions: Exact Julian date of Nisan 1, 605 (Parker & Dubberstein tables not yet imported).
